    Simultaneous solutions of linear equations in an endofinite module #

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.exists_finite_agreement_of_artinian {E : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_3} [Ring E] [AddCommGroup M] [Module E M] [IsArtinian E M] (S : Set (AffineSubspace E (ι → M))) (hs : ∀ (t : Finset (AffineSubspace E (ι → M))), ↑t ⊆ S → ∃ (x : ι → M), ∀ B ∈ t, x ∈ B) :
    ∃ (x : ι → M), ∀ B ∈ S, ∀ (t : Finset ι), ∃ y ∈ B, ∀ i ∈ t, y i = x i

    For a product of Artinian modules, a finitely satisfiable family of affine conditions has a point approximated on every finite coordinate set by solutions to each condition. In particular all closed affine conditions hold there.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.IsEndofinite.extend_of_finite_spans {R : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [Ring R] [AddCommGroup V] [Module R V] {N : ModuleCat R} (U : Submodule R V) (f : ↥U →ₗ[R] ↑N) (hn : IsEndofinite N) (localExt : ∀ (B : Submodule R V), B.FG → ∃ (h : ↥B →ₗ[R] ↑N), ∀ (z : ↥U) (hz : ↑z ∈ B), h ⟨↑z, hz⟩ = f z) :
    ∃ (h : V →ₗ[R] ↑N), h ∘ₗ U.subtype = f

    A map from a submodule into an endofinite module extends to the whole ambient module if it extends on the intersection with every finitely generated submodule. The ambient module can have arbitrary dimension.
